_note: casting.json starter (CASTING.md). Fill every <placeholder> (a --go refuses any left), run `casting.py plan`, quote it to the user. Prompts describe what things ARE; never name what must not appear (that pulls the model toward it): such words go in "ban", a build check. Paths are relative to this file; {NAME} expands a snippet from "text" or the built-ins (SHEET, LOCK, KEEP, STATE, FACELESS, GREY, TAIL, PLATE_TAIL, PRE_FACE, PRE_LOC).

text.WHO: a man of about 50 with dark brown skin, a short grey beard, close-cropped hair and deep-set brown eyes
text.WARDROBE: a rust-orange canvas field jacket over a cream henley, olive work trousers and brown leather boots

state-2.prompt: {STATE} soaked from the rain: hair wet, the jacket dark with water. LEFT panel: a front-facing close-up of the head and shoulders, eyes to camera. MIDDLE panel: the full body from the front, the face area left as a soft plain shadow with no features. RIGHT panel: the full body from behind. {TAIL}

costume.prompt: Image 1 is the locked character sheet. A faceless costume detail sheet: {FACELESS} 1 the jacket collar; 2 the boots from the side and from below. {TAIL}

props.prompt: Image 1 shows the world these props belong to. A faceless props sheet: {FACELESS} 1 the jacket collar; 2 the boots from the side and from below. {TAIL}

place-1.prompt: An empty location plate, three-quarter view, no people: a desert field station of corrugated steel and canvas, a clear path down the middle. low warm sun from the left, long cool shadows. 24mm lens. {PLATE_TAIL}

S01.prompt: {PRE_FACE}{PRE_LOC}a medium shot: he walks toward camera down the path, squinting, warm low sun
